prompt.en: The commentators note that the response to this oath is left ____

explanation.en: The essay says the commentators note the oath's response is left unstated; its sense is that what the deniers were promised is true and they shall surely be raised.

anchor.quote: The commentators note that the response to this oath is left unstated

prompt.en: According to the note on verse 2, what did Ubayy ibn Khalaf do before Abu Jahl?

options.en: He scattered the dust of a grave to deny any return.
He snapped a date palm branch and demanded a sign.
He crumbled a bone and jeered that it would live again.
He pointed to the sky and claimed it had cracks.

explanation.en: Qummi relates these verses came down about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crumbled a bone before Abu Jahl and jeered that Muhammad claimed it would live again.

anchor.quote: who crumbled a bone before Abu Jahl and jeered that Muhammad claimed it would live again

prompt.en: According to the passage, the deniers' real problem was not ignorance but denial, since they rejected the truth after it came to them.

explanation.en: The essay says their problem is not ignorance but denial: they rejected the truth when it reached them and fell into confusion, calling the Prophet mad, a magician, and a poet.

anchor.quote: Their problem, the surah adds, is not ignorance but denial: they rejected the truth when it reached them

prompt.en: "There is no water on earth but that the water of the sky has mingled with it." Who said this of the rain?

explanation.en: Asked about the verse on salubrious water, the Messenger of God said there is no water on earth but that the water of the sky has mingled with it.

anchor.quote: there is no water on earth but that the water of the sky has mingled with it

prompt.en: According to the essay's close, how does the passage turn the deniers' objection back on itself?

options.en: The first creation tired God, so the new one is easier.
The ruined nations perished because creation had wearied God.
The deniers doubt because the first creation was never finished.
The first creation did not tire God, so He can restore.

explanation.en: The essay's close turns the denial back on itself: God was not wearied by the first creation, so He is not unable to restore it, yet they still doubt.

anchor.quote: God was not wearied by the first creation, its origination, so He is not unable to restore it

prompt.en: According to the passage, the whisper in man's soul is ascribed to Satan alone, never to the soul itself.

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai ascribes the whisper to the soul itself and not only to Satan, so claiming it belongs to Satan alone reverses his reading.

anchor.quote: the whisper is ascribed to the soul itself, not only to Satan

prompt.en: What alternate reading of the death verse does the passage report as the recitation of the Ahl al-Bayt?

options.en: The throes of death bring the truth
The agony of the truth came with death
This is the promised day of resurrection
This is what you used to shun

explanation.en: The note says Al-Tusi records the Ahl al-Bayt's recitation as 'the agony of the truth came with death,' not the throes of death bringing the truth.

anchor.quote: Al-Tusi records an alternate reading, 'the agony of the truth came with death,' the recitation of the Ahl al-Bayt

prompt.en: The veil is lifted, and the man's sight, long dulled by his absorption in worldly ____, becomes acute.

explanation.en: The essay says the man's sight was long dulled by his absorption in worldly causes, so once the veil is lifted his eyesight becomes acute.

anchor.quote: The veil is lifted, and the man's sight, long dulled by his absorption in worldly causes, becomes acute

prompt.en: In the passage, what does the devil who accompanied the man say at the judgment?

options.en: That God had ordered him to tempt the man
That he will share the punishment with the man
That he did not make the man rebel; the man erred himself
That the man forced him into rebellion

explanation.en: The essay says the companion devil disowns the man at judgment, claiming he did not make him rebel but that the man chose his own far error.

anchor.quote: The devil who accompanied him disowns him: I did not make him rebel, but he chose his own far error

prompt.en: "Rather, He gives them a choice and grants them respite until they repent ... How could He, when He says, 'Your Lord is not unjust to the servants'?" Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked whether God compels people to sin, Imam al-Rida replied that God gives them a choice and respite to repent, and never burdens them beyond their capacity.

anchor.quote: Rather, He gives them a choice and grants them respite until they repent

prompt.en: "My Lord, You promised to fill the Fire and promised to fill me; why have You not filled me when You have filled the Fire?" Who said this?

explanation.en: Asked about Hell's question whether it is full, Imam al-Sadiq described Paradise pleading to be filled as the Fire was, after which God creates a new creation to fill it.

anchor.quote: My Lord, You promised to fill the Fire and promised to fill me; why have You not filled me when You have filled the Fire?

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does Tabatabai read verse 36 about the mightier nations that were destroyed?

options.en: As a promise of reward to the patient
As praise for nations stronger than these
As capping the argument with a threat
As a sign the deniers will be forgiven

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai reads the question about the destroyed nations as capping the argument with a threat, echoing the warning that opened the surah.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai reads this as capping the argument with a threat, echoing the warning that opened the surah

prompt.en: O Hisham, God says in His Book, 'There is indeed an admonition in that for one who has a heart' - meaning ____.

explanation.en: The narration glosses the heart in the verse as the intellect, so the one who has a heart is the one who reasons, not merely an organ.

anchor.quote: God says in His Book, 'There is indeed an admonition in that for one who has a heart' - meaning intellect

prompt.en: According to the passage, the day the caller calls from a close quarter is explained as the Return.

explanation.en: Asked about the caller, the Cry and the day of rising, Imam al-Sadiq answered that it is the Return, which is what the passage states.

anchor.quote: He said: It is the Return.

prompt.en: According to the essay's closing paragraph, what does it say is the Prophet's task toward those who deny?

options.en: To compel them until they believe
To record what the deniers say against them
To withhold the Quran from those who fear
Only to admonish by the Quran those who fear the threat

explanation.en: The essay's close says the Prophet is not there to compel the deniers; his task is only to admonish by the Quran those who fear the threat.

anchor.quote: his task is only to admonish by the Quran those who fear the threat
